data.title: Tumbling Treasury yields set to drag down Indian bond yields
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds are poised to extend gains on Monday, supported by a decline in US Treasury yields on safe-haven demand and stable crude oil prices.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.15% and 7.20%, according to a private bank trader, after ending at 7.1868% on Friday. The yield fell 12 basis points last week, reversing a similar rise in the previous week.

"The momentum should favour bulls, and a test of 7.15% could be on the cards before some consolidation sets in," the trader said.

US Treasury yields tumbled on Friday, with the benchmark 10-year yield posting its biggest weekly decline since early April 2025, as investors rotated out of equities and into safe-haven assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.90%, as concerns over rising corporate spending and debt linked to AI, along with worries about increased scrutiny and slower data-centre expansion following the Democrats' midterm sweep, weighed on sentiment.

The decline in yields also reflects growing expectations that the Federal Reserve could adopt a more measured approach at its December policy meeting.

Meanwhile, Brent crude hovered around $92 per barrel, though concerns about possible US-Iran tensions and buying ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday continued to lend support to prices.

Oil price movements are critical for India, a major importer of crude, because they affect the current account deficit, the rupee and the inflation outlook.

The Reserve Bank of India's next policy decision is due on December 4, and a majority of economists in a Reuters poll expect a 25-basis-point rate hike.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates are likely to decline in line with bond yields.

On Friday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.47%, while the two-year rate (INR2YIBROIS=CC) closed at 6.43%. The more liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.45%, easing below the one-year rate for first time in 18 months.

data.title: Hyundai sales slump in South Korea as Tesla surges
data.description:
Hyundai Motor sold 448,181 vehicles in South Korea from January through September, its lowest domestic total since the 2008 global financial crisis, as buyers turned to Kia, Tesla and imported luxury brands, Korea JoongAng Daily reported on November 22. The figure was 16.3% below the same period a year earlier.

SUVs, Hyundai's most lucrative category, have suffered the steepest drop. Tesla, by contrast, is the top-selling imported brand in Korea and has more than doubled its sales there this year, even though regulators are holding up its attempt to offer Full Self-Driving (FSD). After reaching a high of KRW787,000 ($590) on June 2, Hyundai's stock has shed more than 60% of its value and currently changes hands in the mid-KRW200,000 range. Worldwide, the company sold 2.89mn units, a 7% decline; setting aside the 2020 pandemic year, this is the first time since 2010 that the total has come in under 3mn.

The Palisade suffered a 41.8% decline to 26,989 units, the Tucson slid 39% to 24,209, and the Santa Fe was down 31.7% at 31,146. In October, Kia outsold Hyundai together with its Genesis brand in the domestic market.

'Much of the Santa Fe's demand has moved to Kia's Sorento and design may be one of the main culprits,' said Lee Ho-geun, a professor of future automotive engineering at Daeduk University. 'Korean buyers favor certain designs by segment, like a rugged, masculine look for midsize SUVs. Hyundai ignored that completely, and consumers left [for the Sorento].'

Through October, Tesla's sales in Korea climbed 105%. Only the Kia Sorento outsold the Model Y, which found 78,631 buyers. Once subsidies are applied, the price of the Shanghai-made model can drop to the high KRW30mn range.

However, the American automaker has hit obstacles with its FSD ambitions. Tesla Korea submitted its application by email on October 22, seeking to be exempted from Korea's vehicle safety rules. On November 20, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport declared itself unable to examine the request because the paperwork fell short, Yonhap reported. Apart from three cover pages drawn from Dutch approval documents, the filing held just two pages of technical content, according to the ministry.

The ministry said it had asked Tesla several times for safety validation data, details of US defect investigations and information on sales contracts involving the unauthorised FSD feature. It said it was 'yet to receive a detailed response.'

From January through October, Genesis sold 68,683 units, a 29.4% decline, while competing luxury marques Mercedes-Benz and Lexus attracted more customers in the same months. Its GV90 electric SUV went on sale on November 10 with a price tag of KRW200mn.

Hyundai is counting on hybrids and redesigned models for a recovery. It launched the GV80 Hybrid last month and unveiled a G80 hybrid, and a GV70 version will follow.

'With the new Tucson, the GV80 Hybrid and the new Avante ramping up, along with peak-season demand, fourth quarter sales can recover,' said Kim Chang-ho, an analyst at Korea Investment & Securities.

Priced roughly KRW3mn above the model it replaces, the new Avante sold under half the volume in its first three months that the previous generation achieved following its 2020 debut. The sales committee of Hyundai's union is now demanding that the company revisit its prices.

'Genesis sales may restore some profitability, but that can't be a clear way out of this slump for now,' Lee said.

data.title: C&R Research Advances as a Next-Generation Global CRO with AI and Healthcare Data
data.description:
Driving Clinical Development Leadership Through Global Expansion and Innovation

SEOUL, South Korea, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Founded in 1997, C&R Research (KOSDAQ: 359090) pioneered Korea's contract research organization (CRO) industry. With over 2,800 clinical projects, the company is expanding internationally while positioning AI and healthcare data as new engines of growth.

From a Korean CRO Leader to a Global Clinical Development Partner

As drug development grows more complex and regulatory requirements vary across markets, integrated global capabilities have become essential. Through its operations in the United States, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, C&R Research has conducted multi-regional clinical trials (MRCTs) in more than 25 countries, supporting Korean companies in global trials and international companies in Korea and Asia.

With extensive experience in global regulatory affairs, including U.S. FDA requirements, C&R Research has strengthened its international presence. Global inbound contracts in 2025 reached 2.6 times the 2023 level. In 2026, the company was recognized among the Global Top 50 CROs and Asia-Pacific Top 25 CROs.

Combining Clinical Expertise with AI and Healthcare Data

AI and healthcare data are central to C&R Research's future competitiveness. As technology transforms clinical trial design, patient recruitment and data analysis, digital capabilities have become a key differentiator for CROs.

C&R Research is enhancing its services by integrating AI and healthcare data with its clinical expertise. It is digitizing trial operations through eClinical solutions, exploring AI applications to improve efficiency, and expanding the use of healthcare data in clinical research. By leveraging the expertise of its affiliates Trial Informatics and Mediplexus, the company aims to deliver integrated clinical development services powered by technology and data.

Sustainable Growth Through Global Reach and Innovation

C&R Research plans to broaden its global network and strengthen its AI and healthcare data initiatives, while meeting the clinical quality and operational standards expected by global pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies across diverse markets.

Approaching its 30th anniversary in 2027, C&R Research aims to become a global CRO that pairs clinical expertise with technological innovation to help bring innovative therapies to patients faster and more efficiently.

For more details contact Jisung Myeong (Brand Marketing Specialist/BMS) from C&R Research Inc. at PR@cnrres.com or visit https://www.cnrres.com/en/.

SOURCE C&R Research Inc.

data.title: LANDMARK Unveils Festive Spectacle "Christmas at The Gloucester Hotel" Bringing Central's Heritage to Life This Holiday Season
data.description:
EQS Newswire / 23/11/2026 / 03:00 CET/CEST

Created with acclaimed London-based creative studio CLOSER, the multi-level holiday marvel bridges storied heritage with modern imagination as the centrepiece of Destination CENTRAL

HONG KONG SAR – Media OutReach Newswire – 23 November 2026 – This holiday season, LANDMARK invites guests to check in to a world of timeless magic with "Christmas at The Gloucester Hotel", welcoming visitors at LANDMARK ATRIUM from 20 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. Created in collaboration with acclaimed London-based creative studio CLOSER, the multi-level spectacle marks the studio's first-ever holiday installation in Hong Kong. Merging exceptional craftsmanship, architectural history and artistry, the experience reimagines the glamour of Central's historic 1932 Gloucester Hotel through a storybook lens; HSBC's iconic lions are also collaborating with LANDMARK for the first time, spreading festive cheer. Ushering in a vibrant new chapter for Destination CENTRAL, the installation builds upon the district's cultural momentum, unlocking a refreshed Central Passport featuring stamp-and-win experiences and over 50 dining privileges. Together with Winter Wonderland in Central, presented jointly by Hongkong Land and the Hong Kong Tourism Board (HKTB), Central shines as the city's ultimate festive playground. Rising within LANDMARK ATRIUM, "Christmas at The Gloucester Hotel" revives the glamour of festive travel through an enchanting storybook lens. Paying homage to the historic 1932 landmark that once stood on this very address, the installation reawakens the soul of the original Gloucester Hotel — a defining social destination crowned atop the Gloucester Building, famed for elegant lounges and terraces that drew the city's elite. Today, the spectacle brings the address to life through a charming festive fable: founded by teddy bear hotelier Cornelius Claus — the "Duke of Christmas" — the hotel is reopened today by his grandson, Concierge Edmund "Teddy" Claus. Illuminating The Grand Lobby, a magnificent Baccarat crystal chandelier sets a radiant tone, while the open-access Gloucester Square welcomes all visitors with a carousel, festive bench, and a statue of Cornelius Claus. Adding to the spectacle, a dazzling indoor light show will also take place every 30 minutes, bringing to life the festive spirit of The Gloucester Hotel. Inside, guests with a Stage Pass unlock a world of playful surprises: gliding down a spiral Laundry Chute Slide into the Grand Hall, picking a favourite Christmas tune on the Mezzanine jukebox to bring the hotel's musical band to life with vibrant lights and melodies, or choosing a postcard in the Mailroom to pen holiday wishes, with complimentary mailing courtesy of LANDMARK. Guests can also capture portraits at the photo station and visit Bunny Astor at Café Claus & High Tea Salon, where family crafting workshops — from festive lanterns, neon art, to snow globes — are hosted. Outside in the Piazza, the celebrations continue with live choral and musical performances. In a nod to Central's shared heritage, HSBC's legendary guardians — the famed bronze lions outside the HSBC Main Building, Stephen and Stitt — are collaborating with LANDMARK for the first time, stepping out to join the festive celebrations. Symbolising boldness and bravery through Stephen, and mindfulness and stability through Stitt, the beloved duo unites with The Gloucester Hotel family as charming ornaments among the glittering branches of Christmas trees across LANDMARK, spreading holiday cheer to all. Guests can bring the experience home with exclusive character ornaments from The Holiday Shop. In the spirit of giving, all proceeds from Stage Passes and designated retail sales will be donated to Caritas Hong Kong. Spreading joy across the wider portfolio, Make-A-Wish Hong Kong will host a dedicated charity booth on the Ground Floor of LANDMARK PRINCE'S. Mr. Alexander Li, Head of Asset Management, Hong Kong Central, Hongkong Land Limited, said: "Building on the momentum of our Tomorrow's CENTRAL transformation and Destination CENTRAL, we are delighted to honour LANDMARK's storied heritage of hospitality by reimagining the historic 1932 Gloucester Hotel alongside CLOSER. Through this golden-age spectacle, we warmly invite our entire community and visitors from around the world to check in, feel right at home, and celebrate the magic of the season together." Ms. Faye McLeod, Co-Founder, CLOSER, said: "Christmas is a time of wonder, and our ambition is to create something truly special, crafted with love. Inspired by LANDMARK's rich heritage, we reimagine the Gloucester Hotel as a place of magical exploration for children and adults alike. Every detail is brought to life with artisanal precision and thoughtful storytelling, evoking the glamour of the golden age of travel while capturing the enchantment, curiosity and delight of the festive period." Destination CENTRAL Evolves into a District-Wide Celebration As the second chapter of LANDMARK's Destination CENTRAL, "Christmas at The Gloucester Hotel" anchors the district's holiday spirit as the gateway to an inspiring winter journey. Spreading festive cheer across the neighbourhood, the much-loved Central Passport returns in a refreshed postcard-themed edition designed as a collectible keepsake. Visitors can embark on a citywide stamp trail across designated Central checkpoints, and collect three stamps to enter a lucky draw at the Destination CENTRAL Redemption Counter on 2/F, LANDMARK ATRIUM — with a chance to win up to 66,000 Asia Miles alongside exclusive holiday gifts — while enjoying curated dining privileges at more than 50 participating partners, including Lan Kwai Fong, The Murray, and Ocean Park.

data.title: India's RBI expected to raise rates in December, deliver final hike in February
data.description:
Key points:
  • RBI to raise repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% on December 4, say 56 of 61 economists
  • Majority expect final hike to 6% in February as inflation tops target band

By Pranoy Krishna

The Reserve Bank of India is widely expected to raise its key interest rate to 5.75% on December 4, followed by a final hike in February, a Reuters poll of economists showed, as inflation breaches the upper end of the central bank's 2%-6% target band.

An energy price shock triggered by the war in the Middle East, coupled with uneven and deficient monsoon rainfall, pushed inflation past the RBI's 6% threshold in October for the first time in two years.

Other major central banks, including the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, are also expected to raise rates in December to fight persistently high inflation.

With India's economic growth expected to remain strong, the RBI, which kick-started its rate-hiking cycle last month, has room to tighten policy further, analysts say.

More than 90% of economists, 56 of 61, in a November 13-20 Reuters poll forecast the RBI to hike its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% at the conclusion of its December 2-4 policy meeting.

While three economists expected the central bank to leave rates unchanged, two predicted a larger 50-basis-point increase.

A majority of economists, 34 of 46, also forecast the RBI to follow up with a final hike to 6% in February.

"The inflation outlook has deteriorated in the last few months ... the fact that India is growing much faster than we had expected — could be north of 8% easily — I think that gives the RBI more latitude to prioritise elevated inflation, which has now breached the upper end of the tolerance range," said Dhiraj Nim, senior economist at ANZ.

"There is a clear generalisation of pressures beyond transitory parts of CPI, which are energy and food."

Despite a recent decline in crude oil , prices are nearly 30% above prewar levels, suggesting inflation will remain elevated in the near term.

However, the rupee's turnaround from one of Asia's worst-performing currencies to one of its best-performing could give the RBI space to moderate the pace of tightening. The central bank has spent billions of dollars to defend the currency against the dollar this year.

Still, a cumulative 75-basis-point increase would mark the shallowest tightening cycle in more than eight years.

"The chatter around aggressive rate hikes was only building up because the rupee was under significant pressure just a month ago. At this point, they (RBI) will be a little more comfortable," said Upasna Bharadwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, who expects two more rate hikes.

Bharadwaj added inflation would remain elevated and closer to the 6% mark for the next five to six months.

While inflation was forecast to average 6% in the fourth quarter and come down in the subsequent quarters, it was expected to stay above the RBI's medium-term target of 4% this year and next — a view broadly unchanged from the October poll.

Elevated prices will weigh on household spending and slow economic activity over the coming quarters.

The economy likely grew about 8% on average over the past five quarters, including the one just ended, but is expected to slow to 6.9% this quarter and 6.8% next, the survey showed.

"Growth is improving purely because of government expenditure and, to a certain extent, because of urban consumption ... But (from) this quarter onwards, I don't think these two stories will play as much," said Debopam Chaudhuri, chief economist at Piramal Group.

(Other stories from the November Reuters global economic poll)

data.title: Gentrack Group Lifts Recurring Revenue but Project Delays Weigh on Profit
data.description:
Gentrack Group has delivered 15% growth in recurring revenue for the year to September, but delays in utility software projects pushed earnings sharply lower despite a stronger airports business.

Total revenue edged up to A$191.3 million (NZ$231.5m) from A$190.2m (NZ$230.2m), as an increase in ongoing customer payments was largely offset by fewer one-off implementation projects.

Recurring revenue reached A$147.9m (NZ$179m), up from A$128.4m (NZ$155.4m), while non-recurring sales contracted by 30% to A$43.5m (NZ$52.6m).

The software provider, which serves energy and water utilities alongside airports, maintained its medium-term growth ambitions but stopped short of offering financial guidance for 2027.

Utility Delays Hit Earnings

The divergence between those revenue streams was most pronounced in Utilities, where established contracts continued to grow even as work on new customer installations arrived more slowly than expected.

Recurring Utilities revenue benefited from earlier client wins to increase 12% to A$126.5m (NZ$153.1m), but non-recurring revenue fell 43% to A$27.1m (NZ$32.8m) after completed projects were not replaced at the same pace.

Rather than pull back from product development and international expansion during the lull, Gentrack maintained investment, adding to the pressure on operating returns.

EBITDA, excluding acquisition costs, declined to A$13.6m (NZ$16.5m) from A$23m (NZ$27.8m), with the reduction concentrated in Utilities.

Net profit after tax fell to A$6.3m (NZ$7.6m) from A$17.3m (NZ$20.9m), against a prior-year result that had also benefited from larger foreign-exchange gains.

Airport Growth Counterweight

While Utilities absorbed the project delays, Gentrack’s Veovo airport software business expanded across established customers and new markets, providing the clearest operating growth in the group.

Including a contribution from Dubai Technology Partners (DTP), which joined the business in June, Veovo recorded 24% revenue growth to A$37.7m (NZ$45.6m).

Excluding DTP, sales rose 15% to A$34.9m (NZ$42.2m), helped by a 26% increase in recurring revenue to A$19.8m (NZ$24m) as earlier contract wins and upgrades flowed through.

The airport division added NAV CANADA as a customer and completed a passenger-flow technology rollout across 25 Saudi Arabian airports, while the DTP acquisition broadened its products and delivery capacity.

Elsewhere, the acquisition of Factor in May added pricing and forecasting software to Gentrack’s g2 utility platform, with trials under way among existing clients and prospective customers.

Conservative Capital Allocation

Those purchases are influencing capital allocation as much as product strategy, with Gentrack choosing to preserve funds for further acquisitions rather than resume shareholder distributions.

Cash stood at A$40.6m (NZ$49.1m) at September’s end, compared with A$70.1m (NZ$84.8m) a year earlier, after the group invested A$33.6m (NZ$40.7m) in the two acquisitions.

Gentrack reported no external debt and ruled out both a dividend and a share buyback, keeping its balance sheet available for growth opportunities.

New customer selections included Momentum Energy in Australia and Zeusa in the UK, while deployment work on g2 continued for utility clients in several markets.

Although management expects organic growth in both Utilities and Veovo during 2027, it says guidance is premature and retains a medium-term ambition of more than 15% compound annual revenue growth and EBITDA margins of 15% to 20%.

data.title: Iron ore slides on weakening China demand, falling steel margins
data.description:
Iron ore prices slid on Monday, dragged down by persistently falling demand and shrinking steel margins in top consumer China.

The most-traded iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange fell 0.69% to 651.5 yuan ($97.57) a metric ton, as of 0153 GMT.

By 0143 GMT, the benchmark December iron ore (SZZFZ6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.25% lower at $88.25 a ton. The contract has stayed well below a key psychological level of $90 for five straight sessions.

Demand for the key steelmaking ingredient remained weak as thinner steel margins and lacklustre steel demand curbed the restocking appetite for feedstocks.

The average daily hot metal output, a gauge of iron ore demand, slipped for six consecutive weeks, down 0.3% from the week before to an eight-month low at 2.3 million tons as of November 19, data from consultancy Mysteel showed.

Meanwhile, only around 10% of Chinese steelmakers were operating at a profit as of November 19, versus 38% in the same period a year before, according to Mysteel data.

However, analysts at broker Yongan Futures said: "Ore prices will likely bottom out following a wave of steep falls, given that its valuation has stayed relatively low."

Coking coal NYMEX:ACT1! and coke (DCJcv1), other steelmaking ingredients, dropped 0.86% and 0.15%, respectively.

Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange were broadly weaker. Rebar shed 0.63%, hot-rolled coil slipped 0.83% and stainless steel lost 0.84%.

($1 = 6.6770 Chinese yuan)

data.title: ANT, BABA, PANW, TTWO, ZS: Why Retail Traders Couldn’t Take Their Eyes Off These Stocks Last Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in its Nov. 19 IPO, with total funding reaching $107.3 billion. 
  • Palo Alto Networks gained 6.5% after strong Q1 revenue and $4.5 billion AI startup acquisition.
  • Take-Two Interactive stock fell 7% despite Grand Theft Auto VI’s $3.79 billion first-day sales. 

Anthropic's (ANT) record-breaking market debut, Alibaba's (BABA) AI spending squeeze, Palo Alto Networks’ (PANW) acquisition and raised outlook, Grand Theft Auto VI's blockbuster launch and CrowdStrike's reported Zscaler (ZS) talks kept retail traders glued to their screens last week.

Anthropic's $81.3 Billion IPO Sets New Record

Anthropic’s Nov. 19 IPO raised $81.3 billion, making it the largest IPO ever. The company priced shares at $83 each, above its initial target range of $70 to $78. Including a separate $26 billion investment from tech companies, the total reaches $107.3 billion, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion. The IPO alone surpassed SpaceX’s $75 billion offering in June.

Bloomberg reported retail orders of $115 billion to $120 billion, ahead of the $100 billion-plus SpaceX drew. William Blair's Arjun Bhatia started coverage with an ‘Outperform’ rating, saying AI is still early and Anthropic will claim a bigger share of enterprise budgets over the next decade.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Alibaba Beats Revenue Estimates But Legal Risks Loom

Alibaba stock dropped 14% to its worst week in a year after beating on second-quarter sales but stumbling on profit. Revenue rose 10% to $40.498 billion, edging past the $40.410 billion estimate. Adjusted earnings per ADS climbed 86% to $1.21, missing the $1.64 estimate. However, Alibaba’s Capital spending jumped 60%, and free cash flow swung to an outflow of RMB34.47 billion ($5.14 billion), worse than last year's RMB21.84 billion.

Freedom Broker lowered its price target to $180 from $200 but maintained a ‘Buy’ rating. Barclays cut its target to $155 from $200 while keeping its ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm said stricter U.S. chip restrictions could actually benefit the company in the long run. A proposed shareholder lawsuit over a Singapore-linked company suspected of helping China access restricted Nvidia chips adds to investor concerns.

Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Palo Alto Networks Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue Outlook

Palo Alto Networks stock recorded a weekly gain of 6.5% after lifting its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $14.52 billion-$14.57 billion from $14.10 billion-$14.20 billion. The cybersecurity provider’s Q1 revenue jumped 39% to $3.44 billion, beating analysts' expectations of $3.31 billion.

The company also agreed to buy AI startup Applied Compute in a $4.5 billion all-stock deal. Applied Compute helps businesses build and run AI models on their own systems, giving them more control over data, customization and costs. BMO nudged up its price target on PANW to $425 from $415, noting accelerating and recurring revenue. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

GTA VI Generates Record $3.79 Billion In First-Day Sales

Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar said "Grand Theft Auto VI" generated an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day sales after 32.5 million pre-release units. For scale, "Grand Theft Auto V" took in $800 million in its first 24 hours back in 2013.

Wells Fargo now sees 65 million for fiscal Q3. Yet TTWO stock dropped 7% over the week. The analyst said Take-Two must show the momentum can become lasting bookings and earnings growth through GTA Online. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

Zscaler Shares Reverse Three-Week Losing Streak On Buyout Buzz

Late Friday, Bloomberg reported CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire Zscaler. Zscaler stock reversed a three week loss and ended the week 1.2% higher. Talks may not lead to a deal, and neither company has commented. The talks come as demand for cybersecurity services grows due to rising hacking threats and new AI-related risks.

Roth Capital kept a Neutral rating and $170 price target but said the deal would fill CrowdStrike's network-security gap and sharpen its fight with Palo Alto. At a CyberArk-style multiple, Roth estimated Zscaler could fetch $300 a share. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’.

data.title: Welspun Living shares, up 100% in 2026, are in focus after ₹3,200 crore capex plan
data.description:
Shares of Welspun Living Ltd. will be in focus on Monday, November 23, after the company approved a capital expenditure plan of up to ₹3,200 crore at its wholly owned subsidiary, Welspun Home Solutions Ltd. (WHSL), to expand manufacturing capacity and strengthen backward integration.

The proposed investment will support the addition of 29,000 metric tonnes of terry towel manufacturing capacity, along with new spinning and weaving facilities. The plan also includes setting up a research and development (R&D) centre.

To fund the expansion, Welspun Living will invest up to ₹800 crore in WHSL through the subscription of either 8% non-cumulative optionally convertible redeemable preference shares (NCOCRPS) or optionally convertible debentures (OCDs), in one or more tranches.

WHSL will raise the remaining ₹2,400 crore through borrowings from banks and financial institutions.

The capital expenditure is expected to be completed by December 31, 2028.

Welspun Living said the proposed investment in WHSL would constitute a related-party transaction, as the subsidiary is wholly owned by the company. However, the transaction will be carried out at arm's length. The promoter, promoter group and group companies have no interest in WHSL other than through Welspun Living.

WHSL reported a turnover of ₹537.78 crore in FY26, compared with ₹224.98 crore in FY25 and ₹199.52 crore in FY24. Its net worth stood at ₹298.51 crore as of March 31, 2026.

The proposed investment is intended to fund the subsidiary's capacity expansion and support Welspun Living's growth strategy at the consolidated level. The company said the activity falls within its main line of business.

Welspun Living shares settled 4.21% higher at ₹263.80 on Friday. The stock has gained around 100% so far in 2026.

data.title: Gold, silver recover after sharp sell-off: Key triggers for prices this week
data.description:
Gold and silver prices recovered in early Asian trade on Monday, November 23, after suffering sharp losses last week, as investors reassessed the interest rate outlook ahead of key US inflation data and fresh signals from the Federal Reserve.

Spot gold rose around 1.1% to $3,578.24 per ounce, recovering from a 9% decline last week that pushed prices to a 14-month low. Silver gained 2.6% to $42.21 an ounce after falling 15% in the previous week.

The rebound comes after a sharp correction in precious metals, with investors weighing the outlook for US interest rates, inflationary pressures and the strength of the dollar.

Why are gold and silver prices recovering?

The rebound follows a sharp sell-off in bullion last week, which pushed gold and silver to their lowest levels in more than a year. The correction prompted some investors to return to the market to buy at lower prices.

In India and China, physical gold demand reportedly picked up last week as price declines attracted bargain hunters and investors looking to accumulate bullion.

However, the recovery may also reflect short-term buying after the steep decline, rather than a reversal of the broader trend.

US inflation data, Fed rate outlook in focus

Investors are closely tracking the US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data due on Wednesday (November 25). The report could offer fresh clues on the Federal Reserve's interest rate trajectory and influence bullion prices.

Markets are also assessing hawkish comments from Fed officials, including concerns over persistent inflation and whether interest rates need to remain higher for longer.

Higher interest rates generally weigh on gold and silver as they increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. Expectations of tighter monetary policy can also support the US dollar, making dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

How did gold and silver perform last week?

The correction was sharp across both international and domestic markets.

  • Gold: MCX December futures fell by ₹14,927, or 11%, last week to close at ₹1.21 lakh per 10 grams.
  • Silver: MCX December futures declined by ₹28,496, or 16.2%, to ₹1.47 lakh per kg.
  • International gold: COMEX gold fell by $370.9, or 9.5%, to $3,515.40 an ounce.
  • International silver: Silver declined by $8.05, or 16.4%, to $41.07 an ounce.

The sell-off was attributed to profit booking, a stronger rupee, hawkish Fed commentary and weakness across broader financial markets, including AI-linked stocks. Silver also faced pressure from declines in industrial metals, including copper and zinc, given its industrial demand exposure.

What should investors watch next?

The near-term direction of precious metals will depend on US inflation readings, Federal Reserve signals, dollar movements and global market sentiment. While the latest rebound offers some relief after last week's steep losses, analysts cited in the supplied reports expect volatility to remain elevated and further downside cannot be ruled out.

The shortened US trading week due to Thanksgiving could also reduce liquidity and amplify price swings.

-With agencies inputs

data.title: The AI Build-Out Is Sucking Up Resources and Crowding Out the Rest of the Economy — WSJ
data.description:
By Justin Lahart

The artificial-intelligence build-out has become the major force behind U.S. economic growth. But in doing so it is also pushing other areas of the economy aside.

Anthropic's tumultuous performance dragged down the whole market on Friday, just a day after debuting the largest public offering ever. The selloff, combined with problems at chip maker Nvidia, underscored risks to an economy so dependent on AI for growth.

The build-out is far-reaching. There is spending on data-center construction, on semiconductors and computing gear, on generators, backup batteries and cooling systems. Hotels near data centers are seeing revenue growth rise. Even snowmobile-maker Polaris said it was seeing strong demand for off-road vehicles from contractors building data centers.

"The tentacles of AI are remarkable," said UBS economist Jonathan Pingle. He estimates that the AI boom has accounted for more than half of the nation's economic growth over the past year.

Columbia University economist Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh estimates that nearly $1.3 trillion will go into the AI build-out alone in the U.S. this year. That is more than 1.6 times the gross domestic product of his native Belgium.

U.S. AI-infrastructure companies have issued $212 billion in stock this year through October, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Many of the things AI is vacuuming up — chips and electricity, labor and money — are resources that other businesses also need. The result is a version of what economists call "crowding out."

Chips

The impact is most evident in surging prices for the memory and storage chips — especially those known as DRAM and NAND flash memory — that go into data centers. Some NAND products have more than quadrupled in price over the past year, according to FactSet.

These same components also go into a slew of popular consumer-electronics products, leading to higher prices for items such as iPhones and Nintendo Switches. As chip costs have gone up, "we have had to pass those price increases through to customers," said Nirav Patel, chief executive of personal-computer maker Framework Computer.

The San-Francisco-based company has paused production on chip-powered memory expansion cards it lists at $50 and $125, letting them sell out. The company said that it would have had to raise prices beyond what most customers would willingly pay.

Memory chips also go into a variety of nontech products ranging from dishwashers to karaoke machines and cars. Steve Downing, chief executive at automotive supplier Gentex, told conference attendees this month that higher memory costs create "massive headwinds on the profitability side."

Money

So far this year, the so-called hyperscalers — Alphabet, Amazon.com, Meta Platforms, Microsoft and Oracle — have issued $277 billion in debt, according to Fitch Ratings, which compares with $108 billion for all of last year. On top of that, data centers have also issued billions of dollars of debt.

AI debt has the potential to affect other types of corporate debt, however. AI debt issuance has accounted for about a fifth of debt issuance this year, up from about a 10th in 2025, according to Dealogic and Goldman.

In a recent report, Fitch analysts cautioned that the heavy concentration of AI-related debt could make the broader bond market more volatile. If investors continue to sour on AI debt, Friday's turmoil could spread. Companies in other sectors could end up paying more to borrow, especially those that have to refinance large amounts of debt soon.

Equipment and workers

In addition to computing gear, data centers are investing in equipment such as gas turbines, transformers and circuit breakers to meet their enormous power needs. And because they are willing to pay higher prices, it is harder for utilities to secure the equipment they need.

In some cases, energy-equipment manufacturers are expanding capacity to meet the moment, said Benjamin Boucher, an energy supply-chain analyst at Wood Mackenzie. But because there is so much uncertainty over the staying power of the data-center building boom, manufacturers of massive pieces of equipment such as gas turbines have been hesitant to do so.

Utilities and other companies are also competing with data centers for workers. In areas with high concentrations of data centers, like Loudoun County, Va., the competition is particularly intense.

"In our area, data centers are taking the experienced employees, promising set hours, no on-call and better pay and benefits," said Rodney Baker, general manager of M.E. Flow, an electrical, heating, cooling and plumbing business with locations in northern Virginia. The company has created a training program in an effort to alleviate the shortage of skilled workers.

Housing

Housing is the sector that the AI build-out might be weighing on most heavily. To a degree this is because it relies on many of the same construction materials, equipment and workers as data centers. Spending on data-center construction has risen sharply since the end of 2023, while spending on new single- and multifamily residential construction has slumped.

But the bigger factor could be what AI is doing to the interest-rate environment, according to UBS's Pingle. Because the build-out is both bolstering the economy and, through higher prices for chips and the like, adding to inflation, it is contributing to the Federal Reserve's case for raising rates.

Expectations that the Fed will continue raising rates have, in turn, pushed mortgage rates higher, damping demand in a housing market that was already struggling. The situation is atypical — usually when the Fed is raising rates, the housing market is booming.

"It is an odd feature of this business cycle that the Federal Reserve is going to make a weak sector even weaker," said Pingle, who began his career as an economist at the central bank.

Write to Justin Lahart at Justin.Lahart@wsj.com

data.title: Jensen and Lori Huang Have Amassed a Vast Fortune. We Break Down Their Wealth. — WSJ
data.description:
By Ashlea Ebeling and Juliet Chung

Jensen and Lori Huang had two young children and just six months of living expenses in the bank when he co-founded Nvidia, the chip maker that would turn them into one of the world's richest couples.

The 63-year-old's sudden resignation from Nvidia after his extramarital affairs came to light has put the company into crisis mode, fueling worries about the AI trade that sent tech stocks sliding this week. Nvidia's shares are down 28% since Jensen's ouster, slashing billions of dollars from the couple's wealth. Yet the Huangs still preside over 870 million shares that recently were worth more than $109 billion.

That sum is spread across a mix of trusts and limited liability companies, as well as a philanthropic organization that has quietly become one of the country's biggest private foundations, according to regulatory filings. As is often the case with the ultrarich, the holdings are deployed in ways to preserve wealth, minimize taxes and create a legacy that can carry on for generations.

Despite the low profile Lori Huang has kept as her husband turned into a global celebrity, she is a central figure in their family's financial empire and listed alongside him in much of their holdings.

The couple met as electrical-engineering students at Oregon State University, where Jensen Huang noticed "this super pretty girl," he said on Guy Raz's "How I Built This" podcast earlier this year.

After college, the two worked in Silicon Valley before she gave up her career to raise their two young children as Jensen started Nvidia. In an interview at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, he recalled their leaner days when they "had to live off of whatever money we had in the bank."

He co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and, not long after, they started estate planning.

A living trust

All told, the couple directly and indirectly owns and controls about 3.6% of Nvidia's shares. That includes about 70 million shares Jensen Huang owns directly, and 800 million shares they may be deemed to have shared ownership of, according to Securities and Exchange Commission filings.

The biggest chunk of those shares is held in a living trust.

The Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Living Trust, created in 1995, holds nearly 468 million shares. It is likely a joint revocable trust, which families set up to manage assets while alive and in the hopes of ensuring a smooth transition to heirs at death, said Justin Miller, national director of wealth planning at Evercore Wealth Management. The couple are co-trustees, which typically means they share decision-making over how to invest and spend the money.

Another roughly 133 million shares are held by LLCs of which the living trust is the sole member, according to SEC filings. That might have been done to protect assets from lawsuits, Miller said. Or they might have been set up for future estate-tax-planning moves, he said.

The Huangs also gifted Nvidia shares to irrevocable trusts before their huge run-up in price. Founders often do this to shift any future growth of their shares out of their estates and save on gift and estate taxes.

"That's the most common estate-planning strategy there is. You give it away when it has a low value hoping that it will increase tremendously in value. By doing that, you get the appreciation out of your estate," said Jonathan Blattmachr, a New York estate-planning lawyer.

The couple in 2012 set up an irrevocable trust that holds just over 31 million shares. The beneficiaries of such trusts are often children and even unborn future heirs.

The couple also created an irrevocable remainder trust in 2016 that holds 109 million shares. They had multiple grantor retained annuity trusts, or GRATs, a way to set aside more money for children free of gift and estate tax, that likely fed into the remainder trust. The couple are co-trustees of the two irrevocable trusts, giving the couple fiduciary responsibility over the trusts on behalf of the trusts' beneficiaries.

Lori Huang hasn't publicly commented on her husband's infidelities. In the event of a divorce, the general starting presumption in California, where the Huangs live, would be that assets acquired during marriage and held by a revocable trust, including LLCs, would be split 50-50, unless there is a marital agreement in place that states otherwise.

As a general rule, both of the irrevocable trusts are outside the Huangs' estates, so the assets wouldn't be subject to any marital split, unless one spouse challenged the conditions under which those trusts were formed, Miller said.

Sharing the wealth

The couple's giving through their private foundation has made them major donors in the Bay Area, where they live.

Last year, the Huangs announced a multiyear commitment to the San Francisco Opera. They hosted a private showing of "The Marriage of Figaro" at the opera house on election night earlier this month that included OpenAI founder Greg Brockman, Salesforce Chief Executive Marc Benioff and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan.

Vanderbilt University also announced this summer that it was granted $75 million from the Huangs' foundation to establish a college of art, architecture and design at its San Francisco campus. Other Bay Area grantees have included Stanford University, where an engineering center is named after Jensen Huang, who earned a master's degree there, and the Second Harvest of Silicon Valley food bank.

Lori Huang is listed as the foundation's president, while Jensen Huang is listed as its secretary and chief financial officer. No other officers or directors are listed for the foundation, which holds another nearly 59 million Nvidia shares, according to an SEC filing this year. Those shares legally belong to the foundation.

The gifts so far represent only a fraction of the foundation's assets, which have soared with Nvidia's ascent, from $12.6 million in 2007 to $9.2 billion at the end of 2024, the most recent year for which an Internal Revenue Service filing is available.

That would make the Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation roughly the 13th biggest private foundation in the U.S. as of 2024, according to Jon Bergdoll, of Indiana University's Lilly Family School of Philanthropy.

Other grantees have included Oregon State University, the Asia Society and several mental-health organizations. The foundation has also bought computing power from AI cloud company CoreWeave to give to universities and other nonprofits "to develop open science and AI research," according to an SEC filing.

But the foundation's biggest distributions by far have repeatedly been to one or more donor-advised funds, or DAFs, held at Charles Schwab. In 2024, it gave a total of more than $80 million to DAFs.

For private foundations like the Huangs', DAFs are useful because gifts to DAFs count toward a 5% minimum payout requirement that private charitable foundations are required to make. Funds in DAFs don't have to be distributed to operating charities in a timely fashion, which has drawn criticism.

Write to Ashlea Ebeling at ashlea.ebeling@wsj.com and Juliet Chung at Juliet.Chung@wsj.com

data.title: Basketball Made Magic Johnson Famous. Mark Walter Made Him a Billionaire. — WSJ
data.description:
By Margot Patrick, Shane Shifflett and Justin Baer

NBA superstar Earvin "Magic" Johnson made a killing in the years since retiring from the Los Angeles Lakers in 1996, investing in movie theaters, shopping centers and retail franchises that served predominantly Black and Latino communities.

Yet it took a partnership with an unlikely teammate — Midwest insurance magnate Mark Walter — to make Johnson a billionaire, beginning with an invitation from Walter to invest in EquiTrust Life Insurance.

Looking back, Walter appears the prime beneficiary of the decadelong relationship.

Johnson, as majority owner of EquiTrust, had by 2025 invested $12.3 billion from his company into enterprises controlled by or linked to Walter, who also held a stake in EquiTrust, according to an analysis by The Wall Street Journal. These transactions mirror others involving Walter-affiliated companies lending to Walter-affiliated businesses — deals now under scrutiny by federal authorities for failure to disclose the in-house ties.

Walter recruited Johnson as an investor in Walter's out-of-the-blue 2012 bid for the Los Angeles Dodgers. The success of the $2 billion deal, the most expensive in U.S. sports at the time, relied in part on a similar financing tactic: All but $100 million for the purchase were undisclosed loans from insurance companies run by Walter's financial firm, Guggenheim Partners.

Insurers are allowed to lend to companies affiliated with their owners as long as the insurance companies comply with state regulatory limits. Such transactions are supposed to be disclosed because of the potential for conflicts of interest and might constitute fraud if they aren't. They also pose a business risk: Agencies that rate financial strength can downgrade insurers with many affiliated investments, potentially scaring off customers.

Walter's inviting Johnson to join the Dodgers ownership group was well-timed for the retired basketball player. Johnson had applied his noted work ethic to a childhood dream of business success, yet lenders showed limited enthusiasm for his wider business ambitions. "Mark Walter said, 'You don't need them. Come to me for funding,'" Johnson told the Economic Club of Chicago last year. "So that's what I do."

It paid off for both men. In 2014, Johnson struck a deal to buy a majority stake in Iowa-based EquiTrust, one of Walter's Guggenheim-run insurance companies. In the years since, Walter's insurers invested hundreds of millions of dollars into Johnson's investment funds and lent around $2 billion to expand the retired sports star's insurance group.

Owners also profited. EquiTrust's assets more than doubled under Johnson's ownership to $36 billion by the end of last year, and it paid out $390 million in net dividends from 2015 to 2025. Johnson's portion was around $234 million, based on his share of the company.

During this time, there also was substantial growth in loans to companies tied to Walter. Those loans eventually accounted for a third of EquiTrust's assets, the Journal found. Arizona, where the company is now based, has a limit of 10% for a single borrower.

Johnson isn't accused of any wrongdoing. But he faces the prospect of federal scrutiny for his extensive business dealings with Walter. An entity managed by another longtime Johnson ally, Eric Holoman, is part of the investigation. Holoman ran operations at EquiTrust as president and now serves as CEO. Holoman didn't respond to requests for comment.

Johnson, who served as the public face of EquiTrust, values his unblemished reputation as a success in sports and business. "My brand is everything to me," Johnson said in a 2015 speech at the Stanford Graduate School of Business. "The one thing that could ruin it all is a tainted brand, a diluted brand. And so I want to protect that brand."

Johnson sold EquiTrust to holding company Amistad Financial late last year and is now one of Amistad's investors along with Walter and others. Amistad Financial is one of four businesses being investigated for their role as intermediaries in Walter's insurance-company borrowing, the Journal has reported.

The Securities and Exchange Commission and the U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan are looking at roughly $24 billion in loans tied to Walter and his companies that wound up on the books of two Delaware-based insurers owned by Walter's holding company, TWG Global.

The two insurers — Delaware Life, and Clear Spring Life and Annuity — are now unloading billions of dollars in investments held in Walter-controlled businesses. To raise capital to buy back those assets, Walter is selling prized holdings, including the Lakers, which he bought last year and are being sold in a deal worth $12.5 billion.

The Delaware insurance department overseeing Walter's insurers said this week the companies, their auditors and regulators were all intentionally misled. The state said it was conducting its own investigation in parallel with federal authorities. A TWG spokesman said, "We strongly disagree with any suggestion that TWG misled anyone."

Adding in the $12.3 billion borrowed from EquiTrust and $6.9 billion from its sister company Heritage Life totals more than $43 billion that went to Walter-affiliated businesses, according to the Journal analysis. It couldn't be learned whether those two companies were part of the federal inquiry.

Walter, TWG, Delaware Life, and Clear Spring Life and Annuity have denied any wrongdoing. TWG called the errors in affiliation calculations a "regulatory matter" that has yielded no victims. It didn't respond to requests for comment on the EquiTrust investments or Walter's relationship with Johnson. Group 1001, TWG's insurance subsidiary in charge of Delaware Life and Clear Spring, declined to comment on EquiTrust investments.

Johnson, who hasn't held board or executive roles at EquiTrust, didn't respond to requests for comment. An outside lawyer for the company told the Journal in 2019 that Johnson wasn't involved with internal operations and instead focused principally on distribution and sales.

Amistad Financial's executive committee said the company is independently owned and governed. The committee said Walter is a non-controlling investor in Amistad and holds no board seat, management position or role in investment decisions.

"EquiTrust investments are underwritten under board-approved guidelines by the investment team that has managed EquiTrust's portfolio since 2016 and is now employed by Amistad Financial Group," the committee said.

It said the Amistad insurance companies haven't been asked to reclassify any investments as affiliated- or related-party transactions. "Amistad has not been accused of wrongdoing by any regulator or authority and will continue to operate its insurance subsidiaries for the benefit of their policyholders," the committee said.

'I hate losing'

Iowa-born Walter, CEO of Guggenheim Partners, pursued Johnson to join his bid for the Dodgers when the team went up for sale during bankruptcy proceedings in 2012. Johnson, the 6-foot-9 point guard who steered the Lakers to five NBA championships in the 1980s, later said that six other billionaires, looking for a partner with local clout, had made a similar pitch.

Johnson grew up in Lansing, Mich., and bonded with Walter over their Midwestern roots during a meeting arranged by sports executive Stan Kasten, who joined Walter's bid for the Dodgers. Johnson later said he asked Walter a question that sealed the deal: Are you competitive?

"I hate losing," Walter later recalled replying.

Johnson was also impressed by Walter's deep pockets. "I said, 'I don't want to just do this deal with you, I want to do 10 deals with you,'" he told an interviewer in 2018.

EquiTrust, which was then under the ownership of Guggenheim, Walter and other investors in the Dodgers deal, helped finance the Dodgers purchase in May 2012. The next year, the insurance commissioner in Iowa, where EquiTrust was based, questioned a $400 million line of credit to fund team assets and told the company to reduce it, said people familiar with the matter. By the end of 2013, it was gone, filings showed.

EquiTrust moved its regulatory oversight to Illinois in 2013 and eventually resumed the lending.

Red flags also surfaced inside the company. In 2013 and 2014, EquiTrust's auditor found that about a fifth of the company's invested assets, $2.8 billion, were with affiliated or related parties.

In January 2014, Johnson held a news briefing at the Chicago headquarters of Guggenheim Partners to announce that he was taking a controlling stake in EquiTrust, promising to bring new jobs to Illinois with EquiTrust's move from Iowa.

After the deal was completed in June 2015, EquiTrust dropped the related-party classification of the $2.8 billion in assets. The following month, Walter borrowed $25 million from EquiTrust to buy a stake in Carvana and joined the startup's board, according to filings.

Under a transition contract, EquiTrust kept a Guggenheim executive as the insurance company's CEO until March 2017. During that two-year transition, the EquiTrust board was largely made up of people who had worked at Guggenheim or its related companies. Walter kept a stake of around 8% in EquiTrust, which he wasn't required to publicly disclose.

Johnson didn't take a role in operations, EquiTrust's lawyer told the Journal in 2019. He signed mini-basketballs and took selfies at the 2015 Christmas party in the West Des Moines office.

The Guggenheim Partners asset-management firm invested on behalf of EquiTrust, collecting more than $100 million in fees between 2015 and 2018, according to EquiTrust's filings.

Friends and family In late 2016, EquiTrust wanted to reinsure a chunk of policies. Guggenheim executives selected a newly set up company in the Cayman Islands called Aureum Re. The executives dismissed questions raised by a risk manager about a lack of information about the company and the lack of bids, according to January 2017 emails reviewed by the Journal. The risk manager was forced out shortly after.

The Illinois insurance department also had questions, according to the emails. It turned out that Walter was part-owner of Aureum Re, along with the Guggenheim executive serving as EquiTrust's CEO, Jeff Lange, and Dan Towriss, then-head of Guggenheim's insurance business. Aureum Re's CEO was Towriss's brother, David Towriss, and the controlling owner was a Guggenheim client close to Walter, Argentine investor Diego Ball.

The insurance department later told EquiTrust to sharpen its governance concerning the approval of reinsurance agreements.

Holoman, who had served as EquiTrust president, became CEO in March 2017. He hired his own executives, who learned of an investment portfolio known inside the company as "friends and family." The loans were for Walter and his business associates to make bets on startups, invest in funds and finance other investment opportunities, according to people familiar with the matter.

During a routine financial examination, the Illinois insurance department flagged the so-called friends and family loans, including the one Walter used to buy the Carvana stake. It ordered a chunk of the loans removed to meet state limits, according to a 2018 corrective order viewed by the Journal.

Walter visited EquiTrust's Chicago office in the fall of 2018. He met with Holoman and the company's chief investment officer to propose ways to keep the lending going, according to a person briefed on the meeting.

EquiTrust soon applied to move its regulatory supervision to another state — Arizona this time.

Johnson was getting funding, too. He launched an investing venture, JLC Infrastructure, which raised more than $300 million for two funds, one in 2017 and a second in 2023, from Walter's insurers and EquiTrust. Neither was identified as a related-party investment.

When Johnson had his 60th birthday in the summer of 2019, he tweeted that Walter was one of his most important mentors.

Around that time, Johnson, Walter and other backers launched a new entity, Amistad Financial. In 2023, it bought Atlanta Life in Georgia, which was started more than a century ago by a former child slave.

In September 2024, Holoman petitioned Arizona's insurance department for Amistad Financial to take control of EquiTrust and Heritage Life. The transaction was completed in November 2025. Don Thompson, the former McDonald's CEO, became Amistad's chairman.

In February, Walter's insurers got subpoenas requesting information on investments linked to Walter. A review by the companies led them to redesignate $24 billion as investments in affiliated parties. Walter's insurers set out a plan to substantially reduce the investments.

Walter still had a generous backer. This year, EquiTrust invested billions of dollars more into entities tied to him. In one week in March, 10 newly set up LLCs received $500 million.

METHODOLOGY

data.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, NYT says
data.description:
Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia's recent scandal, kept in contact with an official from China's top spy agency for more than a year during her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

Alice Huang was in touch with an officer from China's Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters has not been able to reach Alice Huang for comment.

Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.

US authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns it smuggled Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China.

Sunday's report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.

That October 29 article touched off a scandal that led to Jensen Huang's resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia's stock price.

Trump administration officials have repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.

US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.

"Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters," Clayton told CNN's "State of the Union" program. "And I'm going to let that investigation play out."

The scandal has also prompted a deeper look at Washington's approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the prized semiconductors.

The affair between the two itself is of less interest, Senator John Kennedy, a Louisiana Republican, told NBC's "Meet the Press."

"I hope he had a good time," Kennedy said on Sunday. "It was the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy."

data.title: Astellas Pharma Earnings to Be Supported by Cost Savings, Product Mix — Market Talk
data.description: Astellas Pharma's cost savings and improvement in its product mix should help its earnings in the coming years, Jefferies analysts say in a note. Following strong 2Q results, the U.S. bank raises its core operating profit forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to 710.3 billion yen, above the company's Y700 billion guidance. The bank expects the fiscal year starting April 2028 to be the trough year for Astellas after prostate cancer drug Xtandi loses exclusivity next year. Management is confident that some of its higher-margin products are growing fast enough to return Astellas to growth soon after that, the bank says. Jefferies raises its target price on Astellas to Y3,200 from Y2,800 and maintains its buy rating. Shares last closed at Y2,751.5. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

data.title: China stocks fall despite government aid as US chip curbs, AI shares rout sour sentiment
data.description:
China shares opened lower on Monday, as regulators' weekend announcement to ease margin trading requirements did not embolden investors jittery over a deepening selloff in global AI stocks, fresh US chip curbs and a stuttering domestic economy.

Friday's Wall Street plunge also soured sentiment in Asia, as did the prospect of further US rate hikes that threaten to tighten global liquidity.

China's blue-chip CSI300 Index was down roughly 1% minutes after the opening bell, struggling near a 17-month low. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.4%.

In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index lost 1.5% to the lowest level in 19 months.

China's yuan and bonds were steady on Monday.

China's three main stock exchanges unveiled plans on Sunday to ease requirements for margin financing to try to stem the market's slide.

But risk appetite remained low after US stocks tumbled on Friday. Rising Sino-US tensions also hurt sentiment as President Donald Trump said on Friday the US would penalize American companies that build data centers overseas, in Washington's latest move to restrict Chinese access to advanced US chips.

Shanghai's tech-focused STAR 50 Index dropped 3%, while the CSI Artificial Intelligence Index lost nearly 1%.

data.title: Commodity Corner: Crude oil slips on supply concerns; gold rebounds as Fed rate hike bets ease
data.description:
Commodity markets traded mixed on November 23, with crude oil prices declining as investors weighed robust crude exports against the risk of escalating hostilities in the Middle East. Meanwhile, gold prices rebounded after suffering their steepest weekly decline in eight months.

Oil declined as traders weighed signs of robust crude exports against the prospect of escalating hostilities in the Middle East.

Brent slipped below $92 a barrel after closing 0.6% higher on Friday, while West Texas Intermediate was near $83.

Gold rebounded from its biggest weekly decline in eight months as traders scaled back bets on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates in the near term.

Bullion rose as much as 2% to around $3,582 an ounce, after falling 9% last week to a 14-month low. Traders are paring expectations of monetary tightening after growing concerns about artificial intelligence spending rippled across markets, sending technology stocks plunging.

Among other precious metals, silver was up 2.6% at $42.21 after tumbling 15% the week before. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

The dollar eased off its highest level in more than a year and a half at the start of Asian trade on Monday, as investor confidence recovered after a selloff last week and traders pared bets that the Federal Reserve could hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month.

The US dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was flat at 103.80, retreating from its highest levels since April 2025.

data.title: Australia Inflation Data Could Deliver Acute Discomfort — Market Talk
data.description: There could come a moment of acute discomfort for Australia money markets on Wednesday if inflation data for October delivers a higher-than-expected shock. Headline inflation is expected to rise to an uncomfortable 4.7%, but the more important trimmed mean measure is forecast to be little changed, landing at around 3.6% year over year. With recent economic data coming in weak, markets are already starting to price in interest-rate cuts next year, so an upward inflation shock would trigger volatility. Reserve Bank of Australia Gov. Michele Bullock said last week inflation risks remain skewed toward a rise. Central bank rhetoric remains hawkish generally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
